summary: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration has upgraded its Complaint Center so people can more easily report suspected violations of federal motor carrier safety and hazardous materials rules. The platform was previously called the National Consumer Complaint Database, and it now has a redesigned website, submission form and search tool. New categories cover property brokers, Entry-Level Driver Training and Training Provider Registry issues, and registration-related fraud. Medical Review Officer and Substance Abuse Professional complaints now fall under a category called Drug and Alcohol Service Agents. Complaints can be filed online or by phone at 888-368-7238 from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET on weekdays. The agency said filing a complaint does not automatically start an investigation or lead to a penalty.

summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Nov. 5 it will provide $1.5 million to help states improve how they notify vehicle owners about open safety recalls. Funded state programs would develop reliable notification methods tied to vehicle registration and renewal, measure how many recalled vehicles get repaired, and document results so other states can adopt successful practices. NHTSA also wants applicants to study how owners respond to different notification methods and track whether repairs follow. The program is not specifically aimed at commercial trucks, but the article notes that better alerts could help carriers and owner-operators plan repairs. States have until Feb. 4, 2027 to apply, and NHTSA has not said which states will receive grants or when new systems might start. The initiative does not set new commercial maintenance requirements.

orig_title: Verisk CargoNet reports higher cargo theft losses despite fewer incidents
summary: Verisk CargoNet logged 547 cargo and supply chain crime incidents in the U.S. and Canada between July and September 2026, a 33% drop from the same period of 2025. Estimated losses still rose 12% to $230.1 million, up from $205.1 million a year earlier. The average value of stolen commodities with documented values climbed about 72%, to $448,456. Year-to-date losses reached $718.9 million, a 39% increase. Fictitious pickups numbered 138, close to the 147 recorded a year earlier, but made up about 25% of reported activity, compared with 18% in the third quarter of 2025. California reported 182 incidents, ahead of New Jersey with 46, Illinois with 40 and Texas with 43. Food and beverage was the top commodity category at 94 incidents, and metals ranked second with 63, including 34 copper thefts.
